state_order: Every 16-hex-digit state is row-major: character 4*r+c is state row r, column c. Round and position indices are zero based.
round_function: Apply the S-box independently to all 16 nibbles.
For round constant rc, XOR rc&0xf into state[0,0], (rc>>4)&0x3 into state[1,0], and 0x2 into state[2,0].
XOR current_tk1[r,c] xor current_tk2[r,c] into state[r,c] for rows r=0,1 only.
For each column with ShiftRows output (x0,x1,x2,x3), MixColumns returns (x0 xor x2 xor x3, x0, x1 xor x2, x0 xor x2).

tweakey_schedule.permutation_semantics: After each round, first set next_tkq[i] = current_tkq[permutation[i]] for q=1,2.
tweakey_schedule.tk1_update: No LFSR is applied to TK1.
tweakey_schedule.tk2_update: After the permutation, apply LFSR2 to next_tk2[i] for i=0,...,7 only; positions 8,...,15 are unchanged.
tweakey_schedule.lfsr2: For nibble bits (x3,x2,x1,x0), LFSR2 returns (x2,x1,x0,x2 xor x3).
tweakey_schedule.round_tweakey: Round r uses current_tk1[i] xor current_tk2[i] at positions i=0,...,7.

related_tweakey_semantics: Execution 0 uses arbitrary master (TK1,TK2). Execution 1 uses (TK1 xor delta_tk1, TK2 xor delta_tk2). Both executions then follow the same schedule.
trail_boundary_semantics: state_boundaries[r] is the state XOR difference immediately before the S-box of round r for r=0,...,12; state_boundaries[13] is the difference after round 12 MixColumns.
